overview: Tianli International Holdings (formerly Tianli Education, stock code 1773) is a Cayman Islands-incorporated, RMB-reporting operator of private K-12 schools in China, with its core business centered on for-profit private high schools (senior secondary, i.e. non-compulsory education, which remains open to for-profit operation and foreign capital under PRC law). Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, the Group operated 58 schools in 36 cities across 16+ provinces as of FY2025 (ended 31 August 2025), serving approximately 54,000 high school students (rising to ~60,000 at the start of the Autumn 2025 semester). The Group also provides ancillary comprehensive logistics services (dormitory/catering), product sales (uniforms, textbooks, supplies) to its student base, and increasingly earns management/franchise fees from entrusted (non-owned) schools, alongside a nascent AI-education technology initiative.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned primarily from tuition and comprehensive educational services for high school students (non-compulsory/for-profit segment, ~52% of FY2025 revenue), supplemented by sales of products (uniforms, books, supplies, ~28%), comprehensive logistical services (dormitory, catering, ~17%), and management/franchise fees from entrusted schools (~3%, growing fastest at +94% YoY in FY2025 as the Group adds asset-light managed schools). Tuition/comprehensive education revenue is highly recurring (annual/semester contracts tied to enrolled students) while product and logistics revenue is largely volume-driven by the same student base, making overall revenue highly correlated with enrollment and tuition rates. Critically, the Group's elementary/middle school (compulsory education) assets were deconsolidated in FY2021 following PRC regulation banning related-party/contractual control of compulsory-education schools -- the remaining self-owned and entrusted school network is overwhelmingly senior high school (non-compulsory), which remains a permitted for-profit, VIE-controlled business.
business_model.customer_type: B2C (families/students) with a growing B2B2C component via entrusted/franchised school management contracts with local governments and school sponsors
business_model.geographic_mix: Concentrated in Sichuan (home province) with expansion across 36 cities in Inner Mongolia, Shandong, Henan, Hebei, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Yunnan, Gansu, Anhui, Guangxi, Guangdong, Shaanxi, Shanghai, Chongqing and Hubei; 100% PRC-domestic operations, RMB functional currency, HKD-listed equity

main_competitors: local/regional public and private high schools
competitive_position.market_position: One of the larger multi-province private high-school network operators in China, with particular strength/brand recognition in Sichuan and increasing presence in lower-tier cities across western and central China; management and franchise business signals ambition to become an asset-light operator/consolidator of the fragmented private high-school sector

moat_factors.description: Strong, consistently high Gaokao (college entrance exam) results and admissions to top-50 global universities support premium tuition pricing and demand, particularly in "developing" (newer) schools showing dramatic improvement from initial intake
Standardized management and teaching systems allow relatively quick replication of quality standards into new geographies, supporting the entrusted/franchise model
Growing cooperation with local governments for entrusted school management and new campus development lowers capital intensity of growth
Multi-year enrollment of students through to Gaokao creates sticky, recurring revenue within a cohort, though year-to-year competition for new enrollment is intense

Self-developed "Qiming AI Companion" large language model (passed PRC generative AI filing June 2025) aims to cut teaching costs internally and create an external SaaS/To-B/To-G revenue stream, but is unproven at scale

weaknesses: Single-country, single-sector concentration in PRC private K-12 education, which carries outsized PRC policy risk

Reliance on VIE/Structured Contracts to control PRC operating schools, as foreign/social capital ownership of schools is restricted -- this is a structural legal risk common to the sector, not unique to Tianli, but material
Geographic/demand exposure to a single province (Sichuan) for its historical core and brand
History of regulatory shock (2021 deconsolidation and RMB1.1bn impairment) demonstrates vulnerability to sudden rule changes
Net current liabilities position (~RMB2.1bn at FY2025) and rising bank borrowings fund continued campus capex

growth_drivers: Organic enrollment growth: high-school student count rose from ~54,000 to ~60,000 (+11%) entering Autumn 2025 semester
Expansion of the asset-light entrusted/management and franchise school model (18 entrusted schools FY2025, rising to 23 by H1 FY2026) -- faster growth, lower capex than self-owned campuses

AI education technology dual strategy: internal cost/efficiency gains (reduced labor costs, better teacher-student ratios) and external commercialization (To B/To G/To C AI products, AI Bootcamp, AI Intelligent Study Hub, AI Classrooms)
Diversification into comprehensive quality education, logistics services and "diversified higher education" to build an integrated education ecosystem

M&A / inorganic growth -- June 2026 agreement to acquire a controlling 51% stake in Tianlai Technology Group (an art-education specialist: art-college exam prep, arts-integrated general education, children's literacy/arts) for a combined ~RMB244.8m (RMB104m secondary purchase + RMB140.8m capital injection)

Planned overseas expansion -- in negotiations for cooperation with reputable educational institutions in the UK, Hong Kong and other regions, partly to demonstrate compliance with Sino-foreign cooperative schooling qualification requirements

Reversal of prior impairments as previously written-down PP&E (from deconsolidated/affected schools) regains utility -- e.g., RMB100m reversal in FY2025 after obtaining art-training operating licenses for certain tuition schools

business.description: Nearly all revenue derives from PRC private high-school education concentrated in Sichuan-anchored, multi-province network; demographic decline in school-age population in parts of China is a long-term headwind
Revenue and brand are closely tied to continued strong Gaokao results; a reputational or academic-performance setback could pressure enrollment and pricing

FY2025 saw an RMB8.8m goodwill impairment at a Gaokao-repetition school (Sichuan Fengming Niepan) due to a new Gaokao/admissions model reducing enrollment -- shows vulnerability of niche acquired assets to policy/curriculum changes

Large related-party balances (~RMB1.7bn at FY2025) and continuing connected transactions (School Construction Framework Agreements, Structured Contracts) with chairman Luo Shi-affiliated entities raise governance and capital-allocation scrutiny, even though independent directors and auditors confirm compliance with caps and terms each year

financial.description: RMB2.1bn net current liabilities at FY2025 (RMB2.4bn FY2024); management represents going-concern is appropriate given operating cash flow and unutilized banking facilities, but this is a recurring disclosure

Bank borrowings grew from RMB2,053m (FY2024) to RMB2,379m (FY2025) to RMB2,536m (H1 FY2026); finance costs rose 44.5% YoY in FY2025 partly due to cessation of interest capitalization; gearing ratio (borrowings/total assets) rose from 20.1% to 23.9%
Continued capex (~RMB400m/year) for new self-owned school construction and campus upgrades; FCF only turned durably positive from FY2023
RMB functional currency with HKD-listed equity and some USD/HKD cash balances; no hedging policy in place

regulatory.description: The 2021 Implementation Regulations for the Law for Promoting Private Education banned related-party/contractual control (and thus for-profit operation via VIE) of compulsory education (elementary/middle school) and non-profit pre-school; this forced Tianli to deconsolidate ~30 affected schools with a ~RMB1.09bn impairment and a loss on deconsolidation in the FY2021 stub year. The regulations remain subject to interpretive uncertainty at national/local levels (no classification management rules issued as of the FY2025 and H1 FY2026 reports), and management states it continues to monitor and assess ongoing impact. While senior high schools (Tianli's core remaining business) are currently NOT subject to the same for-profit/VIE prohibition as compulsory education, there is residual uncertainty the regulatory perimeter could tighten further over time. This is the single largest overhang on the stock and is related to, but distinct from, the better-known 'double reduction' after-school tutoring crackdown of 2021 that destroyed the K-12 tutoring sector -- Tianli is not an after-school tutoring company and was not directly hit by double reduction; its exposure is specifically to the private/for-profit schooling law, which remains a still-evolving regime.

PRC law restricts foreign ownership of schools; Tianli controls its PRC operating entities via Structured Contracts (VIE), a structure inherently subject to enforceability and policy risk common across PRC education/tech issuers

The PRC Foreign Investment Law (effective 2020) does not explicitly address VIE/contractual-control arrangements; the Company acknowledges uncertainty as to whether such structures could eventually be captured by future rules

Company has adopted a compliance plan (partnering with reputable international institutions, exploring overseas cooperation) to demonstrate it meets qualification/quality requirements as a foreign investor under PRC Sino-foreign cooperative schooling regulations

macro.description: Private school tuition is a discretionary household expense sensitive to PRC macro conditions, youth unemployment concerns, and consumer confidence, though demand for quality education has historically proven relatively resilient

Declining birth rates in China are a long-term structural headwind to school-age population, though the high-school-age cohort reflects births from roughly 15-18 years earlier and net migration to Tianli schools from public/other private schools can offset this for a period

macro.risk: China/Hong Kong equity market sentiment and geopolitical risk
macro.description: HKEX-listed China small/micro-cap with inherent country risk discount; investor sentiment toward Chinese education names remains scarred by the 2021 tutoring crackdown even though Tianli's model differs

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Private K-12 (particularly senior high school) education in China continues to see demand from families seeking better Gaokao outcomes than available in oversubscribed public schools, especially in lower-tier cities; however the sector operates under a tightened and still-evolving regulatory perimeter since 2021, and demographic decline is a multi-year headwind for new enrollment growth nationally
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate; tuition/education spending is relatively defensive vs. general consumer discretionary, but new campus expansion and capex are cyclical with credit conditions and local government cooperation appetite
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- Group carries ~RMB2.4-2.5bn of bank borrowings funding campus construction; finance costs are a meaningful and growing line item (RMB124.8m in FY2025, +44.5% YoY)
key_input_costs: Construction and land-use costs for new campuses
Food/catering and dormitory supplies (procurement cost of products)

recent_developments.event: Revenue grew 14.2% YoY to RMB2,142.8m; profit for the period grew 21.0% YoY to RMB471.4m, but gross margin fell 2.4pp YoY to ~35.2% and most of the profit increase was attributable to a one-off ~RMB81.8m reversal of impairment losses (art-training licenses obtained for previously written-down schools) -- excluding this, profit was roughly flat YoY per independent commentary (Bamboo Works)

Agreed to acquire an aggregate 51% controlling stake in Tianlai Technology Group, an art-education specialist, via a RMB104m secondary share purchase plus a RMB140.8m capital injection (combined ~RMB244.8m), to be consolidated as a subsidiary; expands the education portfolio into art-focused training and college entrance exam art prep

Chairman and CEO Luo Shi made multiple open-market share purchases (~HK$2.6-2.8/share), lifting his direct/indirect stake to ~44.77% (935.5m shares); company conducted on-market share buybacks (200,000 shares) under a January 2026 repurchase mandate (up to 209.2m shares authorized)

Revenue +8.1% YoY to RMB3,588.9m; net profit +16.5% YoY to RMB648.1m (profit attributable to shareholders RMB664.3m per task data); results boosted by a RMB100.0m reversal of PP&E impairment (art-training licenses) but partly offset by a new RMB8.8m goodwill impairment at a Gaokao-repetition school; bank borrowings rose to RMB2,379m; dividend payout ratio maintained at 30% (DPS 9.68 RMB cents, +17.3% YoY)

399 high school graduates admitted to world top-50 universities (up from 272 in 2024, +127 students), including Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial College London and UCL; ~90% of established-school graduates met PRC undergraduate admission thresholds and ~58% met first-tier university thresholds

Self-developed "Qiming AI Companion" large language model passed PRC's national generative AI service filing, enabling formal commercial rollout of AI Bootcamp, AI Intelligent Study Hub and AI Classroom products

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (28 Nov 2025) and H1 FY2026 Interim Report

items.target: ~60,000 students enrolled at start of Autumn 2025 semester
items.notes: Up ~11% from ~54,000 at start of Autumn 2024 semester; disclosed as a forward enrollment figure rather than formal guidance, but is the primary volume driver management points to for FY2026 growth
No explicit forward payout guidance given, but ratio has been held flat at 30% for two consecutive years

items.target: Dual-wheel strategy: expand school network (self-operation + entrustment) and scale AI education technology (internal cost reduction + external To B/To G/To C commercialization)
items.vs_prior: new framing (introduced in FY2025 annual report outlook)
items.notes: No specific quantitative revenue/margin targets disclosed for the AI business or school network expansion; qualitative strategic guidance only

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Luo Shi's FY2025 statement emphasized continued nationwide school-network expansion (self-operation and entrustment dual-channel model), diversification into comprehensive quality/logistics/higher-education services, and an 'internal and external dual circulation' AI strategy to cut labor costs and create new growth curves via AI product commercialization (To B/To G/community C services). No specific numerical FY2026 revenue, margin, or capex guidance was disclosed in the filings reviewed; management's H1 FY2026 commentary (per secondary sources) continued to tout AI-driven growth even as underlying (ex-impairment-reversal) profit was roughly flat.

bull_case: Core business (private senior high schools) sits in a segment of PRC education regulation that remains open to for-profit, foreign-capital-backed operation, unlike the compulsory-education and after-school-tutoring segments that were effectively destroyed by 2021 regulatory crackdowns -- the worst of the regulatory shock may already be behind the company
Consistent double-digit enrollment growth (+11% into Autumn 2025) and strong, improving Gaokao outcomes support premium brand positioning and pricing power
Shift toward an asset-light entrusted/franchise school model and management fee income lowers incremental capital intensity and improves scalability of growth

Free cash flow has turned durably positive since FY2023 after years of heavy campus-construction capex, supporting a rising, well-covered dividend (30% payout, DPS +17% YoY in FY2025) and share buybacks

Strong insider alignment -- chairman/CEO Luo Shi has been an active open-market buyer of stock in 2026 at prices well above where the stock traded for parts of 2025, alongside company buybacks, both of which signal management's confidence at current depressed valuation (reported trailing P/E around 2x per screening data)
Optionality from AI education technology initiative (Qiming AI Companion) and new art-education vertical (Tianlai Technology acquisition) could diversify revenue beyond the core school network
bear_case: China private education remains a politically sensitive sector; the 2021 Implementation Regulations' classification rules are still not finalized years later, leaving meaningful residual uncertainty about how far restrictions could eventually extend, even to the non-compulsory segment Tianli now depends on almost entirely

VIE/Structured Contracts structure used to control PRC operating schools is an inherent legal and enforceability risk shared across PRC/HK-listed education and tech issuers, and was the direct mechanism forcibly unwound for the compulsory-education schools in 2021

Headline profit growth has been significantly inflated by one-off, non-cash impairment reversals in both FY2025 (RMB100m) and H1 FY2026 (RMB81.8m) related to previously written-down assets regaining licenses/utility; underlying (ex-reversal) profit growth has been much more modest to flat, a pattern investors and analysts (Bamboo Works) have flagged explicitly

Rising bank borrowings (RMB2.4-2.5bn) and finance costs (+44.5% YoY in FY2025), combined with a persistent net current liabilities position (~RMB2.1bn), keep balance-sheet and refinancing risk elevated even as the business funds continued campus expansion

Large related-party balances (~RMB1.7bn) and continuing connected transactions with chairman-affiliated entities (school construction framework agreements, Structured Contracts) raise governance and capital-allocation concerns typical of founder-controlled PRC issuers

Deep value/out-of-favor stock: extremely low reported P/E (~2x) and wide analyst target dispersion (HK$5.3-6.3 vs. trading levels reported in the HK$1-3 range across sources) suggest the market continues to apply a heavy discount for China-education-sector and governance/structure risk that may persist regardless of fundamentals
China's declining birth rate is a multi-year structural headwind to the addressable school-age population nationally, even if Tianli can still gain share regionally in the near term
